name: Closing cut under the rise
look: A cut-out lifted from the closing product photograph rises into place. The photograph takes over in the same position. The complete closing sentence and its action stand together from the first frame.
reduced: The finished composition: the markup as the page writes it, nothing moving.
phone: The same rise and cut at full width: the cut-out fitted to the width less 16px margins, starting low and rising whole onto the subject's place in the portrait crop, the closing photograph's own portrait crop with its own floor line and the subject whole, a shallower dip (phoneDip 0.1, lowered where it would sink the subject's foot under the band) so the crop keeps its height and the subject stays whole above the band, the line over the action on the short band at the foot, the caption left out (it would sit on the cut-out). phone: 'rest' gives the finished composition, the closing photograph a screen tall with the band, the line and the action.
place: The end of the page: the order, the booking or the visit, straight after one quiet section. The footer after it is a designed section of its own and follows the finished frame: leave `foot` unset (it pulls the element it names over the stage's foot, so it suits only a page that ends on the scene). Once per page, never right after another scene. Pages that sell or show one ordinary physical thing: a teapot, a jug, a stool, a lamp, a bottle, a dish, a garment.
content: One full-colour closing photograph of the subject in place: the very object standing clear of its surroundings (a distinct colour or a plain ground behind it, so it can be masked) on a floor, a table top or a counter that meets the wall, trees or sky behind on a clear line, with a calm area or room at its foot for a short band; landscape 2400px wide or more, and a portrait crop as its own <source> in which the subject stays whole (or one file framed with --ccr-object-portrait). The rising cut-out is masked from that same photograph (keyed or traced, transparent PNG or WebP, the object only, nothing of the table under it), so the cut lands the very thing back in its own room; never a drawing, never a second photograph of a lookalike. On the img and each <source>: data-horizon (that file's floor line, 0-1) and data-subject (the subject's centre across and its foot, 0-1). Words: the page's last sentence (not the brand name, no invented history) of 6-12 words in two or three phrases, each a .ccr-step; one action of 2-4 words (an order, a booking; never an email address or phone number), visible with the whole sentence; an optional caption of 2-6 words naming the object. --ccr-wall and --ccr-floor set to the photograph's wall and floor (or tint 'auto'); --ccr-band-ink with 4.5:1 or more on the band. Flat tints only: no fade through black or white, no glow, no gradient.
options: The held scroll is capped at 1 screen plus the stage. See the demo for framing options.
